CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain at the end of right middle finger.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 41-year-old female who presents with pain at the tip of her right middle finger following a motor vehicle accident. She was rear-ended while stopped at a four-way stop approximately four to five days ago. The other driver appeared to be texting. In response to the accident, the patient became angry and attempted to make a gesture at the other driver but struck the ceiling of her car with her right middle finger instead. She denies any other injuries from the accident. The car sustained minimal damage to the trunk. Pain has persisted for four to five days at the tip of the right middle finger.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger. Pain elicited with palpation at the distal phalanx. No pain with palpation at other locations on the finger. General exam otherwise normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger shows distal phalanx fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Prescribed tramadol 50 mg every six hours as needed for pain (8 tablets dispensed). Placed in finger splint. Follow-up x-ray in two weeks. Patient counseled that tramadol is safe to take with her current digoxin therapy.
